mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% in a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 40% of the instances where FEDFUNDS increased by more than 0.25% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals a weakening demand in the housing sector, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown and thus negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where HOUST dropped by more than 5% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month indicates a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending power diminishes.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where UNRATE increased by more than 0.5% in a month.

mechanism_narrative: An unexpected decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a supply shock, which can lead to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as production slowdowns ripple through the economy.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are positive in more than 60% of the instances where INDPRO dropped by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) over three consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where RSAFS increased over three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) grow by more than 200,000 in a month, it indicates a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer confidence and spending increase.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where PAYEMS increased by more than 200,000 in a month.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, it signals inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, which can lead to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate higher nominal growth.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 60% of the instances where FEDFUNDS is below 1% and CPIAUCSL increased by more than 0.3% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) grows by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.2% in the same quarter, it signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending improve.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 grows > 2% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decreases > 0.2% in the same quarter
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns of S&P 500 are negative in more than 40% of the instances where GDPC1 grew by more than 2% quarter-over-quarter and UNRATE decreased by more than 0.2% in the same quarter.
